subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt persisted provider-level cooldown state for inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials, or keep billing cooldowns limited to auth profiles and document profile migration as the supported path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the durable inline-key cooldown namespace and fail-closed upgrade behavior are auth-provider policy and compatibility choices that should be accepted before the linked PR lands.

options.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
options.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys get the same billing/auth cooldown protection as profile-backed credentials.

options.title: Keep profile-only cooldowns
options.body: Close the implementation path as not planned and document moving inline keys into auth profiles as the supported workaround.

options.title: Request narrower design
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers specify the exact cooldown identity, persistence, fallback, and recovery behavior they want.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
recommendation.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys get the same billing/auth cooldown protection as profile-backed credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: Among the observed routing candidates, steipete has adjacent auth-resolution history and repeated issue-timeline routing for this auth-provider policy decision.
